subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP thread messages bypass busy reply-operation/channel admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior crosses message-delivery ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback semantics, so maintainer intent is needed before another repair lane starts.

options.title: Refresh the admission PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, rebase or replace it, and preserve no-visible fallback plus terminal-session recovery semantics before merge.

options.title: Limit steering to explicit controls
options.body: Keep ordinary messages queued for now, document command-only steering, and avoid changing default admission behavior until the routing contract is redesigned.

options.title: Split a Discord ACP follow-up
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 canonical for general steer admission and track a narrower Discord ACP thread issue if that surface needs separate ownership.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, rebase or replace it, and preserve no-visible fallback plus terminal-session recovery semantics before merge.
